text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + tail latency observed for inference endpoints in us-west-3a (az: usw3a). 5xx rate spiked to 6.2% over the last 5m, p99 latency ~3.1s. Auto-route fallback triggered once. Paging on-call.

pagerduty: Paging maya (oncall) — critical.

maya (oncall): I’m on it, grabbing metrics and starting triage. Which fleets are hitting errors?

devon: Seeing errors predominantly from hosted/text-gen routes -> model rdx-13-3b. Errors look like gRPC downstream EPIPE + connection timeouts from a subset of instances in usw3a.

maya (oncall): running quick health check: `kubectl -n inference get pods -l fleet=rdx-13-3b -o wide` -> shows 4/12 ready on nodes in usw3a, rest healthy in other AZs.

ops-lead: Customer impact: small percentage of routed requests (~3.8% of total platform traffic) are failing or hitting >2s. Dedicated customers in us-west may see increased error rate. Notifying CS.

sarah-cs: Notified a handful of enterprise customers via the shared incident channel; collecting severity. Will escalate if >5% impacted.

maya (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) Increase routing weight away from usw3a via smart-router to 0. 2) Initiate instance drain for suspected bad hosts. 3) Force-kv-cache warm on target AZs to reduce cold token latency.

devon: Runbook commands: `POST /v1/routing/override {"region":"us-west-3","az":"us-west-3a","weight":0}` (internal API). I pushed a temporary override to send 100% traffic to other AZs, monitoring now.

infra-bot: ROUTE_OVERRIDE applied by devon at 2026-03-17T14:05:12Z, previous policy preserved as fallback.

maya (oncall): Metrics: error rate in usw3a falling from 6.2% -> 1.1% within 90s of override. p99 latency for affected routes trending down.

devon: Observed node-level logs from two hosts in usw3a: repeated kernel-level NIC reset events + gRPC connection errors: 
```
Mar 17 14:02:03 host-137 kernel: net: eth0: link reset
Mar 17 14:02:04 host-137 inference-service[pid]: grpc: conn error: write tcp: connection reset by peer
```
Looks like transient host NIC problems causing session resets and KV cache churn.

maya (oncall): Drained the 2 suspect hosts and started reprovisioning. Eviction confirmed. Autoscaler kicked ephemeral replacements in other AZs.

ops-lead: Customer impact update: SLO alerts triggered but overall % impacted dropped to ~0.9%. Continuing to monitor for residual errors.

sarah-cs: Updating customers: "We detected a transient network impairment in one AZ and have shifted traffic. Services restored for majority; we’ll follow up with a detailed RCA." :thumbsup:

infra-bot: ASG/autohealing events: 2 instances terminated, 2 replacements launched in us-west-3b at 2026-03-17T14:07:40Z.

maya (oncall): Can we keep override in place until next maintenance window? I want to ensure KV caches repopulate and no regression when we return traffic.

devon: I set the override with timed expiry 60m. If all metrics stay green we can start gradual reweight in 30m with canary at 10%.

ops-lead: Next steps: handoff to night oncall (maya -> devon) at 14:20 UTC. Prepare short blurb for post-incident and include kernel NIC resets + autoscaling remediation.

maya (oncall): Handoff: current state: override active, errors in usw3a <1%, suspect root cause: host NIC flapping causing gRPC conn resets and KV-cache churn. Actions taken: routing override, drained bad hosts, replacements launched. Followup: collect host NIC metrics, vendor if recurrence.

devon: I’m taking next shift. Will watch for reweight canary at ~14:35 UTC. Leaving logs and the small grep snippets in the incident ticket.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: sev=high -> degraded -> monitoring. Ticket created: INC-2026-0384.

maya (oncall): Thanks team. Closing pager. :white_check_mark:
